problem_text:
A logistics coordinator must allocate shipments into identical cargo pods. Shipments:

* Component Alpha: mass 52 units
* Component Beta: mass 58 units
* Component Gamma: mass 56 units
* Component Delta: mass 64 units
* Component Epsilon: mass 32 units
* Component Zeta: mass 55 units
* Component Eta: mass 64 units
* Component Theta: mass 52 units
* Component Iota: mass 70 units
* Component Kappa: mass 30 units
* Component Lambda: mass 52 units
* Component Mu: mass 31 units
* Component Nu: mass 67 units
* Component Xi: mass 60 units
* Component Omicron: mass 62 units
* Component Pi: mass 69 units
* Component Rho: mass 57 units
* Component Sigma: mass 44 units
* Component Tau: mass 33 units
* Component Upsilon: mass 49 units
* Component Phi: mass 62 units
* Component Chi: mass 64 units
* Component Psi: mass 42 units
* Component Omega: mass 68 units
* Component Aleph: mass 64 units
* Component Beth: mass 43 units
* Component Gimel: mass 37 units
* Component Dalet: mass 62 units
* Component He: mass 55 units
* Component Vav: mass 37 units
* Component Zayin: mass 65 units
* Component Het: mass 33 units
* Component Tet: mass 46 units
* Component Yod: mass 50 units
* Component Kaf: mass 51 units
* Component Lamed: mass 33 units
* Component Mem: mass 58 units

Each cargo pod can sustain a maximum load of 100 units. The objective is to allocate every component into a pod, ensuring the aggregate mass within any single pod does not surpass its capacity, while employing the minimal possible number of pods. Every component must be placed into exactly one pod.
